title: 5 As compared to 1970, all heads of crime indicated an increase in 1980 except 'Criminal Breach of Trust' which declined by 8.8 percent in 1980 over 1970. The heads of crime to register an increase in 1980 over 1970 were 'Other IPC offences (86.4%), 'Riots' (56.5%), 'Dacoity' (54.5%), 'Cheating' (41.2%), 'Murder' (41.0%), 'Robbery' (38.5%), 'Kidnapping & Abduction' (34.5%), 'Thefts' (27.8%), 'Counterfeiting' (27.7%) and 'Burglary' (0.2%) which resulted in an increase of 43.2 percent in total cognizable crime in 1980 over 1970. The highest increase in 1980 over 1979 was noted under 'Counterfeiting' (58.1%), followed by 'Murder' (8.8%), 'Dacoity' (8.3%), 'Riots' (8.2%), Other IPC Offences (4.5%), 'Kidnapping & Abduction' (3.6%), 'Robbery' (2.8%), and 'Thefts' (1.3%). Whereas a decline was recorded under 'Criminal Breach of Trust' (6.1%), 'Cheating' (5.2%) and 'Burglary' (1.1%), resulting in an increase of 2.4 percent in total cognizable crime under IPC in 1980 over 1979. As compared to quinquennial average of 1975-1979 the incidence of crime in 1980 registered an increase under 'Riots' (31.5%), 'Dacoity' (20.1%), 'Murder' (20.0%), 'Kidnapping & Abduction' (10.8%), 'Other IPC offences' (21.7%), 'Counterfeiting' (9.8%), 'Robbery' (8.6%), and 'Thefts' (3.3%). The crime heads to register a decline were 'Criminal Breach of Trust' (10.1%), 'Cheating' (8.5%) and 'Burglary' (8.2%). The total cognizable crime, however, recorded an increase of 10.3 percent during the same period.
